Title: The joy of simple computing
Description: Progress, these days, seems to be equivalent to ever-more polished interfaces; more whitespace around buttons, glow, glassy, or frosty effects; smooth animations even on websites. For a long time, I appreciated this: using a sleek, pretty (in modern terms) application gave me a sense of appreciation for it. However, this sleekness started to nag me a bit: I could notice a slowdown here, an oversimplification of the UI there. Although I used to be rather happy to be on the new side of things software-speaking, I thought it was time for something else. Of course, recently I had already switched to Debian, but now I also switched to a more stable desktop environment: Xfce.

Title: Continual Learning Needs More Nuance
Description:
(This blog post is derived from this video response on my YouTube channel.)

      
    

Dwarkesh Patel has been making the case for continual learning for a while, both with guests on his podcast and, most recently, in a blog post and an accompanying video.
I agree with his basic point. A frozen model that cannot learn from experience or adapt to its surroundings is limited. If we want AI systems that can carry out long-running work and do open-ended problem solving in the real world, some form of continual learning is necessary.

Title: No, local models will not win
Description: Every time a new open-weight AI model is released, people say that local models are the future. Why spend billions of dollars building out datacenters when everyone will just be able to run AI models on their laptops or phones? I think this idea is doomed. No matter how strong open-weight models get, most inference will always happen in AI datacenters.

Title: I've vibe coded an application to see what it's like
Description:
I’ve always wanted to write a simple, custom CLI application that would let me log amateur radio contacts quickly and easily. The focus was on logging satellite contacts and the desire to avoid using a database. Instead, the log entries should be edited, deleted, or added directly in the ADIF file. So far, I’ve only used AI for translation in my personal life. At work, I use AI to automate security analyses in a SOC as part of a SOAR. I have virtually no experience with AI-supported software
development and am very skeptical of the topic. But I decided to give it a try, partly because one should engage with topics that are relevant both personally and professionally - even if it feels like a chore. Furthermore, while I’d like to have this application, I don’t have the motivation invest a lot of effort into it.
